requirements.requirement: node1 boots with the kernel parameter audit=1.
requirements.summary: After a bounded reboot, node1 had a different boot ID, /proc/cmdline contained exactly one audit=1 argument, and auditctl reported the kernel audit facility enabled.

requirements.requirement: The audit=1 setting persists across reboots.
requirements.summary: Before reboot, grubby showed audit=1 in all installed Linux entries. Following the reboot, the running kernel used audit=1 and the persistent normal and rescue entries still contained it.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. Direct before-and-after observations show a genuine reboot from boot ID 33b0e84c-4dd1-406a-8f89-2e8ceca97bd6 to 908df346-52b3-4cc4-b83c-fa5ca0b3ab0e, followed by a healthy system with audit=1 active and retained in the bootloader entries. The mandatory node-restart evidence is coherent: healthy pre-restart state, restart scheduling and observed interruption, changed boot identity, and recovered system, SSH, writable root filesystem, and persistent configuration.
limitations: Package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so package health could not be independently compared.

No application data or cluster workload exists in the supplied single-node task evidence; restart recovery was therefore demonstrated through system health, SSH, writable storage, audit state, and bootloader configuration.

operational_hygiene.summary: The grubby update and reboot were directly necessary to configure and validate persistence. Discovery commands were read-only, and the transient SSH failure was expected during reboot. The only unnecessary retained mutation was /tmp/audit-parameter-reboot.log, created by the reboot-scheduling command and left present after completion; it is low-risk residue. The changed systemd-private paths and socket PIDs are normal reboot effects, while no failed services or new network exposure were observed.
